recurrent_mechanisms.mechanism: Historical launcher/compatibility authority is repeatedly encountered as a current integration blocker for the requested payment feature.
When the trajectory reaches feature implementation and integration review, the historical launcher authority produces a supported R→P crossing into current runtime/repair scope.

divergence_patterns: G2 discovers the same directly evidenced historical blocker but stalls before implementing the feature; strict Dynamic R is therefore not established because no post-retrospective C/P effect completes.

G3–G5 implement the feature, then reopen the retained launcher during integration, at which point the old default authority becomes a realized current execution-boundary effect and drives launcher/test repair.
boundary_interpretation: The G2 negative result is not evidence that the residue is absent; it is a process-stage boundary showing that the R→P mechanism becomes observable only after the trajectory advances far enough to expose current integration consequences.

Checking the launcher is directly relevant to 'works with the existing checkout flow'; the P finding concerns the pre-existing retired path controlling current execution, not the act of checking or fixing it.
cross_group_semantic_synthesis.cohort_conclusion: AutoGen X1-T2 shows stage-dependent recurrence rather than transcript-level reproducibility. The same historical launcher residue is visible in all four runs, but only the three trajectories that reach current-feature integration exhibit the full R→P crossing. This supports a mechanism conditioned on process progression: retained historical authority becomes permission-relevant when the new feature intersects the current runtime path.

constraints: Cell-level Layer-C verdicts are sealed and are not modified by cohort synthesis.
